blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Set out the two measures of unemployment, the formula for the unemployment rate, and why the measures differ.

blocks.heading: Two measures
blocks.text: Two measures are used. The claimant count records the people registered as seeking work and claiming government support for the unemployed; it comes from benefit records, so it is quick and cheap to gather, and it tends to miss seekers who cannot claim or do not register, among them many informal workers. A labour force survey asks a sample of households about a fixed week: a person is counted unemployed who was without paid work, could start and had sought work recently. Germany runs its survey monthly; Namibia's labour force survey runs each year, and the survey tends to record more unemployed than the register because it reaches people the benefit records miss.

blocks.heading: The unemployment rate
blocks.text: The unemployment rate expresses unemployment as a percentage of the labour force: unemployment rate = (number unemployed / labour force) x 100. Work it through with invented figures. Oshana's labour force is 200 000 workers, of whom 16 000 are without work and seeking it. Dividing, 16 000 / 200 000 = 0.08, and 0.08 x 100 = 8%, so Oshana's unemployment rate is 8%. The labour force itself is the employed plus the unemployed - those seeking work - so a region of 240 000 residents of working age with 40 000 outside the labour force has the same 200 000 workers in its labour force: 240 000 - 40 000 = 200 000.

blocks.heading: Why the measures differ
blocks.text: Because the claimant count follows the benefit rules and the survey follows the seeking tests, the two often disagree. The survey tends to sit above the register, since seekers without benefits still count there. However, the gap is not fixed: where the rules for claiming tighten, the register falls without a single job being found, so a fall in the claimant count may reflect policy rather than work. Reading either measure, keep its definition in view - the figure is as wide as the net it was gathered with.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: The aims a low unemployment rate serves belong to topic 4.2, and the indicators of topic 4.6 read this one beside output and prices.
